question: A 60-year-old man comes to the office because of an 8-month history of cough, night sweats, shortness of breath, and fatigue. He has also had a 9-kg (19.8-lb) weight loss during this time. He appears pale. Abdominal examination shows hepatosplenomegaly. His leukocyte count is 80,000/mm3 and his leukocyte alkaline phosphatase level is increased. A peripheral blood smear shows > 82% neutrophils with band forms and immature and mature neutrophil precursors. An x-ray of the chest shows a 9-mm right hilar nodule. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's laboratory findings?
analysis: The patient's symptoms of cough, night sweats, weight loss, and hepatosplenomegaly, along with the leukocytosis and increased leukocyte alkaline phosphatase, suggest a myeloproliferative disorder. The presence of a right hilar nodule raises suspicion for a possible underlying malignancy. The peripheral blood smear showing a high percentage of neutrophils and immature neutrophil precursors is characteristic of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). The leukemoid reaction is less likely given the specific findings of immature cells and the context of the patient's symptoms. Therefore, the most likely cause of this patient's laboratory findings is chronic myeloid leukemia.
